name: Solenne Atelier AutoDry Stormweave Rain Cape
description: A floor-sweeping rain cape in ivory-white smart-fabric that sheds water on contact and returns to a pressed, dry state within forty seconds via embedded micro-thermal filaments activated by body heat. Cut with a high Mandarin-Andean collar and a rear pleat that opens cleanly for wings or dorsal geneware. Worn at Spire level as a casual weather layer — the fact that it costs more than a Circuit worker's monthly wage is entirely the point.
functionality: Self-drying smart-fabric cape with body-heat-activated micro-thermal reset; rear pleat accommodates wing and dorsal geneware.
what_it_says: The rain doesn't touch this person — not really, not in any way that matters.
story_hooks: A cape matching this description was left folded on a Shelf bench in Tier 1 last winter — no identification, no surveillance footage of who left it.
The AutoDry filament network can theoretically be reprogrammed; a Shelf hacker claims to have a method that turns it into a passive surveillance mesh.
